answer: Behavioral plume correlation. Each agent action scatters a trace signature (timing, request mix, tool order); independently registered identities that emit near-identical traces get clustered. A mirror graph of cross-account co-movement flags clusters, and a vine of shared low-level resources links them into one suspect unit. Attacker cost: every extra identity needs genuinely divergent behavior plus distinct infrastructure, raising per-identity upkeep roughly to the cost of running a separate real agent.
